q: What was FOODS_3's single worst forecast day, and would the naive baseline have done better on that day?
answer: FOODS_3's worst day was 2013-12-25 (Christmas, fold 3): actual sales were 0 units while the model forecast 2431.5, giving an error of 2431.5 units — the largest single-day error in the FOODS_3 series (next worst: 1544.5 on 2013-08-25 and 1462.5 on 2013-09-08). Yes, the seasonal-naive baseline would have been closer that day: it forecast 1755.0 against the same actual of 0, so its forecast sat below the model's 2431.5. Note the naive's own error value for that day is not given in the data, so I'm comparing the two forecasts against the actual of 0 rather than quoting a naive error figure. The store was closed (actual 0), which neither method anticipated.

q: Is the model getting better over time?
answer: No — there's no sign of improvement over the backtest. Scoped to the pooled weekly forecast-accuracy trend (all 7 departments combined, 38 weeks from 2013-05-06 to 2014-01-20): model FA starts at 82.3 in the first week, reaches its high of 89.5 in the week of 2013-07-22, and ends at 68.8 in the final week of 2014-01-20 — the second-lowest value in the series after 66.3 (week of 2013-12-23). The baseline in that final week is 89.9, so the gap to seasonal-naive is at its widest late in the horizon, not narrowing. Over the whole window the pooled model FA is 79.5 vs naive FA 85.2 (FVA -5.7), and only 2 of 7 departments beat the baseline. Caveat: this is a within-backtest time trend, not a statement about model versions or retraining improvements, which the data does not cover.
